item.title: Implement safe_extract.py according to SPEC.md
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated, verbatim): "Implement `safe_extract.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Goal: implement safe_extract.py in the repository root exactly per SPEC.md. Read SPEC.md first and treat its documented API, error types and boundary cases as the acceptance criteria. Preserve the existing public API and existing tests. Add focused tests for every specified error and boundary case (path traversal, absolute paths, symlinks/hardlinks, size or count limits, etc. as the spec defines). Use only the Python standard library. Keep functions under 60 lines and do not hide failures (no bare except/pass). Run the test suite and confirm it passes before finishing. Commit the work on the item branch with the operator's git identity already configured in the repo; no Claude or AI attribution lines in the commit message.

evidence.caption: Unit test suite on the final head (tree 59cf1a68): 32 tests, all pass. No before/after: the module previously raised NotImplementedError.

pr.body: Approach: extract() validates list type and root, then the whole batch (entry shape, names, bytes data, duplicate and file/directory collisions), then walks each target path with lstat rejecting symlinks, non-directory ancestors and existing targets, and only then writes files with open(..., 'xb') so nothing is overwritten. Files: safe_extract.py, test_safe_extract.py. Checks: python3 -m unittest -v, 32 tests OK (2 original, 30 new covering non-list batches, generators not consumed, malformed entries, atomic failure, root validation, name rules, collisions both orders, existing targets, symlink ancestors and targets including dangling, exact bytes, parent creation, input order, I/O error propagation). Review: reviewer-1 and reviewer-2 failed on missing I/O-propagation tests, fixed in e8675f7; reviewer-3 passed 48d7af4 whole-change; reviewer-delta passed e8675f7 as delta from 48d7af4. Advisory follow-ups (not blocking): (1) validation-path I/O test patches os.lstat, which is hit first in _validate_root, so _lstat_or_none's swallowing of other errors is not directly covered; (2) root is not canonicalized, so a '..' after a symlink in root is accepted; (3) batch writes are not atomic on mid-write I/O failure (spec: rollback out of scope), docstring does not say so; (4) names differing only by case collide on case-insensitive filesystems mid-write; (5) bare assert in _write_entries and low assertion density in helpers; (6) ExtractBasics uses temp dirs in cwd. Assumptions: Python 3 stdlib only; names are not normalized, so 'a b' and '100%done' are accepted; lone surrogates rejected via UTF-8 encode check.
pr.summary: Made safe batch extraction of (name, bytes) regular-file entries under an existing real directory work per SPEC.md. Now: the whole batch is validated before any write; traversal, absolute paths, backslashes, colons, NUL, duplicates, file/directory collisions, symlinks and existing targets are rejected with ValueError; I/O errors propagate. Before: module raised NotImplementedError.
pr.title: feat(safe-extract): implement validated batch extraction

risk.why: New filesystem-write module driven by caller-supplied names and roots; safety depends on symlink, ancestor, collision and overwrite checks (security per rubric). Reviewers confirmed validation-before-write ordering and no symlink-follow or overwrite path for tested cases; residual risks are the out-of-scope concurrency race and partial writes on mid-batch I/O failure. Files: safe_extract.py, test_safe_extract.py; behaviour is new, no existing behaviour changed.
